title: Ham & Potato Chowder
subtitle: a thick, creamy potato chowder with smoky ham and sweet corn: the best use for leftover ham
imageAlt: A white bowl of creamy potato chowder with diced ham and corn on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for two, plus 4 bowls for lunches

breakdown: Flour, dried thyme, bay leaf, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: Leftover Christmas or Easter ham is perfect here; otherwise a cooked ham steak.
Taste before salting at the end: ham and broth are already salty.

items.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
items.note: peeled and cut in 1.5 cm dice

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium. Cook the onion, celery and carrots 6–7 minutes until soft.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth a little at a time.

steps.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps.text: Add the potatoes, bay leaf and dried thyme, bring to a boil and simmer, partly covered, 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.

steps.title: Thicken more
steps.text: Discard the bay leaf. Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the chowder.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in the ham, corn, milk and pepper and heat 5 minutes, without boiling, until steaming hot, 74°C (165°F). Taste and add salt only if it needs it.

fixIt.fix: Mash more of the potatoes, or simmer a few minutes uncovered.

fixIt.problem: Too thick after a night in the fridge
fixIt.fix: Stir in milk or broth as you reheat.
Add more milk and a few more diced potatoes, and simmer until tender.

saleTip: Ham steaks are often $4–5 at No Frills; after Christmas or Easter, use leftover ham for free.
swap: Bacon: fry 6 chopped strips first and use 2 tbsp of the fat instead of butter.
leftovers: Thickens overnight; loosen with milk when reheating.
doneness: Potatoes tender; chowder steaming hot. Cooked ham reheated to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested ham and potato chowder methods (Canadian Living, Canadian Pork): a roux-thickened broth with potatoes, finished with ham, corn and milk.
prepAhead: Make up to 2 days ahead; it thickens, so add milk when reheating.
reheat: Over medium-low, stirring often, with a splash of milk, until steaming hot; don't let it boil hard or the milk can separate.

basic.note: Ham, potatoes and onion in a creamy broth.

fancy.note: Finished with cream and topped with old cheddar.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: add the cream with the milk.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Top each bowl with a little cheddar.

plating: Cheddar over the top so it melts.

why.0-6: Yukon Golds hold their shape but some break down to thicken the chowder.
why.0-11: Milk goes in last and never boils, so it stays smooth.

funFact: Chowder comes from the French 'chaudière', the cauldron Breton fishermen cooked in; Atlantic Canada has been making it for centuries.

keeps.note: potatoes and milk go grainy when frozen

pairs: made for the leftover Christmas ham
